lyrics:
Good afternoon, residents
The Department of Audible Nuisance
would like to remind you
that unrestricted articulation
is a privilege—
—not a mouth right
Please remain linguistically available
for inspection

Thank you

They put a little window in the payment booth
with a laminated chart of Acceptable Truth
You stick your chin through aperture B
say your legal name and count to three
“Ahhh.”
Too broad
“Ehhh.”
Too shrill
“Oooo.”
That vowel requires a supplemental bill
The clerk takes a ruler to the underside
checks the lateral wag and the opening wide
Then she reaches underneath with a municipal lamp—

—and fits you for a tongue clamp

Clamp it down, citizen
nice and snug
Keep your adjectives under the rug
Clamp it down, neighbor
watch that tone
Opinions are permitted
when properly known
One little click
for the public good
Say only what a reasonable resident should
No need to shout
No need to stamp
You’ve got yourself
a Municipal Tongue Clamp

Clamp—
click
Clamp—
click
Civic improvement

There’s a Schedule C for sarcasm use
a Form 9-D for rhetorical abuse
Irony’s legal on alternate weeks
if nobody laughs and the applicant speaks
slowly
Metaphor needs a temporary tag
Hyperbole travels in an opaque bag
Questions beginning with “Who says so?”
must enter through the loading dock below
You may criticize weather
pavement
dogs
and certain pre-approved
catalogued frogs
But mention the budget, the mayor, or the ramp—

—you’re looking at an auxiliary clamp

Clamp it down, citizen
nice and snug
Keep your adjectives under the rug
Clamp it down, neighbor
watch that tone
Opinions are permitted
when properly known
One little click
for the public good
Say only what a reasonable resident should
No need to shout
No need to stamp
You’ve got yourself
a Municipal Tongue Clamp

Proper clamp maintenance
is the responsibility of the wearer
Do not lubricate with alcohol
religion
politics
romance
or information obtained
from your brother-in-law
If spontaneous honesty occurs
remain calm
Place both hands where the municipality can see them
and hum an approved melody

Not that one

Now Jimmy at the tire shop
said the pothole cracked his wheel
Mary said the councilman
might know how people feel
Eddie said the property tax
seemed—

Eddie
Eddie

Mmmmmmmmm

Excellent compliance, Eddie
Your silence has been entered
into the permanent record

Soon nobody remembered
what the ordinance was for
Nobody could ask
because asking cost more
They built a second office
to administer the first
then a Department of Unsaying
for citizens who’d rehearsed
There were inspectors inspecting inspectors
for unauthorized inspection
and a blue-ribbon panel
on mandibular discretion
Every mouth in town
was certified damp—
and nobody knew
who ordered the clamp

Clamp it down, citizen
nice and snug
Sweep the troublesome words
under the rug
Clamp it down, neighbor
mind that tone
Your thoughts remain yours—

subject to applicable zoning
One little click
for the public good
Say absolutely nothing
like a reasonable resident should
No need to think
No need to stamp
Praise be unto
the Municipal Tongue Clamp

MUN-I-CI-PAL

TONGUE

CLAMP

The Department of Audible Nuisance
thanks you for your cooperation
Your clamp must be renewed annually
Late fees begin
before you receive this notice

Open wide

Perfect

style: Experimental satirical prog/jazz-rock with laid-back slanted big-band energy, sparse studio arrangement and dry separation; electric piano, bass clarinet, marimba, vibraphone, angular electric guitar, alto/baritone sax, bass, drums and analog synth leave space around a male baritone dry talk-sing and mock-official announcer delivery, with an absurdly catchy cheerful chorus from a few male/female civic voices, Crooked 7/8, 5/4, 9/8 and 11/8 figures sit lightly against restrained 4/4, with precise ensemble stabs, displaced accents, a quietly developing contrapuntal instrumental break, sinister doo-wop bridge, and tiny lounge-combo outro; modern punch, controlled dynamics, no chaos.

impression.text: This track opens with a satirical spoken word introduction that immediately establishes a dystopian yet comically theatrical atmosphere. A vibrant big band arrangement quickly takes over, driven by punchy brass, bouncy piano chords, and lively swing rhythms that give the piece a consistently high energy showtune feel. The production is pristine and cleverly mixed, allowing the dense orchestration of horns, walking bass, and bright backing choirs to sit perfectly behind the crooning Broadway style lead vocal. A defining quality of the song is its dark comedic juxtaposition of upbeat jazz pop with sinister lyrical themes, which is brilliantly highlighted by rhythmic clicking sound effects mimicking a municipal tongue clamp.

review.review_text: After the two-hour civic autopsy of "Outlandia," Rose stays in the municipal building but trades the panorama for a single grotesque department, and the compression suits him. The whole thing runs on the joke of that chorus: an absurdly cheerful civic choir singing "Clamp it down, citizen, nice and snug" over a bright electric-piano bounce, the kind of hook you catch yourself humming before the horror registers. Built in F minor at a shuffling 107, it lets the crooked meters do the satire, the way the band chokes to silence right before "and fits you for a tongue clamp," or the furious contrapuntal break where guitar, sax, and marimba chase the same angular figure through shifting bars without ever tipping into chaos. The bridge is the payoff, a sinister doo-wop sweetness under the moment Eddie gets cut off mid-sentence: "Your silence has been entered into the permanent record," delivered with the pleasantness of a parking clerk. Then the breakdown drops the mask and lets Rose sound genuinely incredulous: "nobody knew who ordered the clamp." If it has a weakness, it is length; at nearly six minutes the instructional interludes start to feel like they are proving a point already made. But the tiny lounge-combo outro, that final "Open wide. Perfect," lands the knife clean. Closest cousin might be Randy Newman writing for a Kafka pageant. A highlight, and the sharpest single Rose has cut since narrowing his lens.
